title: Understanding SOLID principles in development
content:
Introduction: The 5 golden rules of clean code

The SOLID principles (Robert C. Martin) = basis of maintainable object-oriented code. Objective: Flexible, testable, scalable code.

🔤 S — Single Responsibility Principle

Rule: One class = one responsibility.

❌ Bad

```typescript class User { save() { /* DB */ } sendEmail() { /* Email */ } generateReport() { /* PDF */ } } ```

✅ Good

```typescript class User { constructor(public name: string) {} } class UserRepository { save(user: User) {} } class EmailService { send(user: User) {} } class ReportGenerator { generate(user: User) {} } ```

🔓 O — Open/Closed Principle

Rule: Open for extension, closed for modification.

❌ Bad

```typescript class PaymentProcessor { process(type: string) { if (type === 'card') {} else if (type === 'paypal') {} // Ajout = modification } } ```

✅ Good

```typescript interface Payment { process(): void; } class CardPayment implements Payment { process() {} } class PayPalPayment implements Payment { process() {} } // Ajout = nouvelle classe ```

🔄 L — Liskov Substitution Principle

Rule: Subclass replaces superclass without breaking.

❌ Bad

```typescript class Bird { fly() {} } class Penguin extends Bird { fly() { throw new Error('Cannot fly!'); } } ```

✅ Good

```typescript interface Bird { move(): void; } class Sparrow implements Bird { move() { /* fly */ } } class Penguin implements Bird { move() { /* swim */ } } ```

🧩 I — Interface Segregation Principle

Rule: Targeted small interfaces > large interface.

✅ Good

```typescript interface Workable { work(): void; } interface Eatable { eat(): void; } class Human implements Workable, Eatable { work() {} eat() {} } class Robot implements Workable { work() {} // Pas de eat() } ```

🔌 D — Dependency Inversion Principle

Rule: Depend on abstractions, not implementations.

❌ Bad

```typescript class MySQLDatabase { save(data: any) {} } class UserService { db = new MySQLDatabase(); // Couplage fort } ```

✅ Good

```typescript interface Database { save(data: any): void; } class MySQLDatabase implements Database { save(data: any) {} } class UserService { constructor(private db: Database) {} // Injection } const service = new UserService(new MySQLDatabase()); ```

🎯 Conclusion

SOLID Summary:
  • S: One responsibility per class
  • O: Extend, not modify
  • L: Case-free substitution
  • I: Targeted interfaces
  • D: Abstractions > Implementations
> “SOLID is not a dogma, it is a compass.” 🧭

title: How to properly divide an application into modules or microservices
content:
Introduction: Modularity = maintainability

A well-structured project is easier to maintain, test and evolve.

1️⃣ Identify functional areas

Breakdown by business responsibilities:
  • User (authentication, profile)
  • Product (catalog, inventory)
  • Payment (transactions, invoices)
  • Notification (email, SMS)

2️⃣ Modular structure (Monolith)

``` src/ ├── user/ │ ├── user.controller.ts │ ├── user.service.ts │ ├── user.repository.ts │ └── user.model.ts ├── product/ │ ├── product.controller.ts │ ├── product.service.ts │ └── product.model.ts ├── payment/ └── notification/ ```

3️⃣ Communication rules

  • Public interfaces: Each module exposes clear API
  • No direct DB access: Go through module service
  • Events: Asynchronous communication between modules
Example: ```typescript // ❌ Mauvais import { UserRepository } from '../user/user.repository'; const user = new UserRepository().findById(id); // ✅ Bon import { UserService } from '../user/user.service'; const user = await userService.getUser(id); ```

4️⃣ Microservices Architecture

Each module = autonomous service with its own DB.

Structure

``` services/ ├── user-service/ │ ├── src/ │ ├── Dockerfile │ └── package.json ├── product-service/ ├── payment-service/ └── api-gateway/ ```

Communication

  • Synchronous: REST API / gRPC
  • Asynchronous: Message queues (RabbitMQ, Kafka)

5️⃣ Bounded Contexts (DDD)

Domain-Driven Design concept:
  • Each module has its own business language
  • A "User" in Auth ≠ "User" in Billing
  • No sharing of models between contexts

6️⃣ When to switch to microservices?

Modular Monolith:
  • ✅ Small team (<10 devs)
  • ✅ Simple/medium product
  • ✅ Rare Deployments
Microservices:
  • ✅ Multiple teams
  • ✅ Differentiated scalability (payment ≠ blog)
  • ✅ Frequent and independent deployments

🎯 Conclusion

Well thought out cutting = longevity of the project. Golden rules:
  • Modules by business domain
  • Clear interfaces between modules
  • Monolith first, microservices if necessary
> “Start as a modular monolith, move to microservices when the pain justifies the complexity.” 🏗️

title: When (and how) to adopt a hexagonal architecture
content:
Introduction: Ports & Adapters

The hexagonal architecture (Alistair Cockburn) separates business logic from the outside world. Objective: Infrastructure-independent business code.

1️⃣ The 3 layers

Domain (core business)

  • Pure business rules
  • Entities, Value Objects
  • No external dependencies

Application (use cases)

  • Business logic orchestration
  • Defines the ports (interfaces)

Infrastructure (adaptors)

  • Concrete implementations
  • DB, API, UI, Email...

2️⃣ Project structure

``` src/ ├── domain/ │ ├── entities/ │ │ └── User.ts │ └── value-objects/ │ └── Email.ts ├── application/ │ ├── ports/ │ │ ├── UserRepository.ts (interface) │ │ └── EmailService.ts (interface) │ └── use-cases/ │ └── CreateUser.ts └── infrastructure/ ├── adapters/ │ ├── PostgresUserRepository.ts │ └── SendGridEmailService.ts └── http/ └── UserController.ts ```

3️⃣ Concrete example

Domain

```typescript // domain/entities/User.ts export class User { constructor( public id: string, public email: string, public name: string ) {} } ```

Application (Port)

```typescript // application/ports/UserRepository.ts export interface UserRepository { save(user: User): Promise; findById(id: string): Promise; } ```

Application (Use Case)

```typescript // application/use-cases/CreateUser.ts export class CreateUser { constructor(private userRepo: UserRepository) {} async execute(email: string, name: string) { const user = new User(uuid(), email, name); await this.userRepo.save(user); return user; } } ```

Infrastructure (Adapt)

```typescript // infrastructure/adapters/PostgresUserRepository.ts export class PostgresUserRepository implements UserRepository { async save(user: User) { await db.query('INSERT INTO users...', [user.id, user.email]); } async findById(id: string) { const row = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]); return row ? new User(row.id, row.email, row.name) : null; } } ```

4️⃣ Advantages

  • Easy tests: Mock repositories without real DB
  • Flexibility: Change DB/API without affecting business
  • Longevity: Stable business code even if infrastructure changes

5️⃣ When to use it?

✅ Yes if:
  • Complex business logic
  • Long-term project (5+ years)
  • Need robust testing
  • Infrastructure subject to change
❌ No if:
  • Simple CRUD
  • Rapid prototype / MVP
  • Junior team (learning curve)

🎯 Conclusion

Hexagonal architecture = separation "what" (business) and "how" (infra). Ideal for scalable projects with rich business logic. > “The profession should never depend on technique.” 🔷

title: The essential design patterns to know (Factory, Singleton, Observer, etc.)
content:
Introduction: Proven Solutions

design patterns = reusable solutions to recurring problems. Objective: Avoid reinventing the wheel.

1️⃣ Singleton

Problem: Only one global instance (DB connection, logger...). ```typescript class Database { private static instance: Database; private constructor() {} // Prevents new Database() static getInstance(): Database { if (!Database.instance) { Database.instance = new Database(); } return Database.instance; } } const db1 = Database.getInstance(); const db2 = Database.getInstance(); console.log(db1 === db2); // true ```

2️⃣ Factory

Problem: Create objects according to context. ```typescript interface Payment { process(): void; } class CardPayment implements Payment { process() { console.log('Card payment'); } } class PayPalPayment implements Payment { process() { console.log('PayPal payment'); } } class PaymentFactory { static create(type: string): Payment { switch (type) { case 'card': return new CardPayment(); case 'paypal': return new PayPalPayment(); default: throw new Error('Unknown payment type'); } } } const payment = PaymentFactory.create('card'); payment.process(); ```

3️⃣ Observe

Problem: Notify multiple items of a change. ```typescript interface Observer { update(data: any): void; } class Subject { private observers: Observer[] = []; subscribe(observer: Observer) { this.observers.push(observer); } notify(data: any) { this.observers.forEach(obs => obs.update(data)); } } class EmailNotifier implements Observer { update(data: any) { console.log('Email sent:', data); } } class SMSNotifier implements Observer { update(data: any) { console.log('SMS sent:', data); } } const userRegistered = new Subject(); userRegistered.subscribe(new EmailNotifier()); userRegistered.subscribe(new SMSNotifier()); userRegistered.notify({ user: 'John' }); // Email sent + SMS sent ```

4️⃣ Strategy

Problem: Change algorithm dynamically. ```typescript interface SortStrategy { sort(data: number[]): number[]; } class BubbleSort implements SortStrategy { sort(data: number[]) { // Bubble sort logic return data; } } class QuickSort implements SortStrategy { sort(data: number[]) { // Quick sort logic return data; } } class Sorter { constructor(private strategy: SortStrategy) {} setStrategy(strategy: SortStrategy) { this.strategy = strategy; } sort(data: number[]) { return this.strategy.sort(data); } } const sorter = new Sorter(new BubbleSort()); sorter.sort([3, 1, 2]); sorter.setStrategy(new QuickSort()); sorter.sort([5, 2, 8]); ```

5️⃣ Adapter

Problem: Make two different interfaces compatible. ```typescript // Ancienne API class OldPaymentAPI { makePayment(amount: number) { console.log('Old API:', amount); } } // Nouvelle interface attendue interface NewPaymentAPI { processPayment(amount: number, currency: string): void; } // Adapter class PaymentAdapter implements NewPaymentAPI { constructor(private oldAPI: OldPaymentAPI) {} processPayment(amount: number, currency: string) { // Adaptation this.oldAPI.makePayment(amount); } } const oldAPI = new OldPaymentAPI(); const adapter = new PaymentAdapter(oldAPI); adapter.processPayment(100, 'EUR'); ```

6️⃣ Decorator

Problem: Add functionality without changing class. ```typescript interface Coffee { cost(): number; } class SimpleCoffee implements Coffee { cost() { return 5; } } class MilkDecorator implements Coffee { constructor(private coffee: Coffee) {} cost() { return this.coffee.cost() + 2; } } class SugarDecorator implements Coffee { constructor(private coffee: Coffee) {} cost() { return this.coffee.cost() + 1; } } let coffee = new SimpleCoffee(); coffee = new MilkDecorator(coffee); coffee = new SugarDecorator(coffee); console.log(coffee.cost()); // 5 + 2 + 1 = 8 ```

🎯 Conclusion

Design patterns = common vocabulary between devs. The 6 essentials:
  • Singleton: Single instance
  • Factory: Conditional creation
  • Observer: Pub/Sub
  • Strategy: Interchangeable algorithms
  • Adapter: Interface compatibility
  • Decorator: Dynamic extension
> “Use patterns carefully, not out of habit.” 🔧

title: Manage technical debt intelligently
content:
Introduction: Debt = conscious choice

Technical debt is everything we put off “for later”. It is not bad in itself, but must be controlled and reimbursed.

1️⃣ Types of debt

Voluntary debt (good):
  • Deliver MVP quickly to validate market
  • Defer refactoring to meet the deadline
  • Minimum documentation for prototype
Involuntary (bad) debt:
  • Poorly designed code due to lack of skill
  • No tests because "we don't have time"
  • Uncontrolled duplication

2️⃣ Measure debt

SonarQube

```bash # Installe SonarQube via Docker docker run -d -p 9000:9000 sonarqube # Run project scan sonar-scanner -Dsonar.projectKey=my-project ``` Key Metrics:
  • Code smells: Anti-patterns detected
  • Coverage: % code tested
  • Duplications: Duplicate code
  • Cyclomatic complexity: Function complexity

3️⃣ Document debt

TODO Comments

```typescript // TODO: Refactor - Extract UserService logic // Reason: Mixed responsibilities (SRP violation) // Impact: Hard to test, tight coupling // Priority: High (before v2.0) function createUser(data: any) { // ... } ```

GitHub/Jira Issues

```markdown Title: [TECH DEBT] Extract payment logic to service Description: - Current: Payment logic in controller (violates MVC) - Impact: Hard to test, reuse - Effort: 2h - Priority: Medium - Due: Before v1.5 ```

4️⃣ Pay off debt

Rule of Scouts

> "Leave the code cleaner than you found it." Each PR = 1 small improvement.

Time-boxing

Allocate 20% of sprint time to technical debt:
  • Sprint 2 weeks = 2 days refacto
  • Priority: High criticality debt

Continuous refactoring

```bash # Before feature git checkout -b feature/new-endpoint # During development: improve touched code # Commit 1: Refactor existing code # Commit 2: Add new feature # PR review checks both ```

5️⃣ Prioritize debt

Impact/Effort Matrix: | Impact | Low effort | Strong effort | |--------|---------------|-------------| | **Top** | ✅ Do it immediately | 🟡 Plan sprint | | **Low** | 🟢 Nice to have | ❌ Skip |

6️⃣ Avoid Debt

  • Code reviews: Detect early
  • Automated testing: Safety net
  • CI/CD strict: Blocks merge if quality <80%
  • Pair programming: Knowledge sharing

🎯 Conclusion

Technical debt is like credit: normal as long as you know when/how to repay. Golden rules:
  • Documents any voluntary debt
  • 20% sprint time = refacto
  • Prioritize by impact/effort
  • Measurement with SonarQube
> “The best technical debt is the one you avoid.” 🏗️

title: Create a scalable project from the start
content:
Introduction: Scalability = Anticipation

A scalable architecture manages the increase in load (users, data, traffic) without complete redesign.

1️⃣ Scaling Types

Vertical Scaling (Scale Up)

Increases machine resources (CPU, RAM, disk). Advantages:
  • Simple: no code change
  • No network complexity
Disadvantages:
  • Physical limit (max 128 CPU)
  • Single Point of Failure
  • Exponential cost

Horizontal Scaling (Scale Out)

Add machines/instances. Advantages:
  • No limit (add instances infinitely)
  • Redundancy = High Availability
  • Linear cost
Disadvantages:
  • Complexity (load balancer, sessions)
  • Code must be stateless

2️⃣ Patterns for scale

Load Balancing

Distributes traffic between instances. ```nginx # nginx.conf upstream backend { server backend1:3000; server backend2:3000; server backend3:3000; } server { location /api { proxy_pass http://backend; proxy_set_header Host $host; } } ```

Stateless Applications

Sessions stored in Redis, not in server memory. ```typescript // ❌ Pas scalable (session en RAM) const sessions = new Map(); // ✅ Scalable (shared session) import { createClient } from 'redis'; const redis = createClient(); async function setSession(userId: string, data: any) { await redis.set(`session:${userId}`, JSON.stringify(data), { EX: 3600 // 1h TTL }); } ```

Database Sharding

Divides data between several DBs. ```typescript // Sharding par user_id modulo function getShardForUser(userId: number): string { const shardCount = 4; const shard = userId % shardCount; return `db-shard-${shard}`; } // Query user_id=12345 → db-shard-1 const db = getShardForUser(12345); // db-shard-1 await queryDatabase(db, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=12345"); ```

Caching

Reduces DB load with distributed cache. ```typescript async function getUser(id: number): Promise { // 1. Check cache const cached = await redis.get(`user:${id}`); if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached); // 2. DB query const user = await db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=?", [id]); // 3. Cache result await redis.set(`user:${id}`, JSON.stringify(user), { EX: 600 }); return user; } ```

3️⃣ Message Queues

Processes heavy tasks asynchronously. ```typescript import { Queue } from 'bullmq'; const emailQueue = new Queue('emails'); // Producer: envoie job await emailQueue.add('sendWelcome', { to: 'user@example.com', template: 'welcome' }); // Consumer: traite jobs const worker = new Worker('emails', async job => { await sendEmail(job.data.to, job.data.template); }); ```

4️⃣ Auto-Scaling (Cloud)

Kubernetes HPA

```yaml apiVersion: autoscaling/v2 kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler metadata: name: api-scaler spec: scaleTargetRef: apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment name: api minReplicas: 2 maxReplicas: 10 metrics: - type: Resource resource: name: cpu target: type: Utilization averageUtilization: 70 ```

5️⃣ Monitoring scalability

Critical Metrics:
  • CPU/RAM: Target <70%
  • Response time: p95 <500ms
  • Queue depth: <1000 jobs pending
  • DB connections: <80% pool

🎯 Scalability Checklist

  • ✅ Stateless app (sessions in Redis)
  • ✅ Load balancer in front of instances
  • ✅ Cache (Redis/Memcached)
  • ✅ DB read replicas
  • ✅ Message queue (async tasks)
  • ✅ Auto-scaling enabled
  • ✅ Real-time monitoring
> “Scale early, optimize often.” 🚀

title: Manage logs and errors properly in an app
content:
Introduction: Logs = Black box

Logs are essential for diagnosing bugs in production. Without them, it's impossible to understand what happened.

1️⃣ Log Levels

  • DEBUG: Details for development (disabled in prod)
  • INFO: Normal events (user logged in, payment processed)
  • WARN: Non-critical anomalies (deprecated API used, slow query)
  • ERROR: Serious errors (DB connection failed, payment error)
  • FATAL: Crash application

2️⃣ Structure logs

Structured JSON (no console.log)

```typescript // ❌ Pas exploitable console.log("User John logged in"); // ✅ Structuré, exploitable logger.info({ event: 'user.login', userId: 12345, username: 'john', ip: '192.168.1.1', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() }); ```

Correlation ID

Traces a request through microservices. ```typescript import { v4 as uuidv4 } from 'uuid'; app.use((req, res, next) => { req.correlationId = req.headers['x-correlation-id'] || uuidv4(); res.setHeader('x-correlation-id', req.correlationId); next(); }); app.get('/api/users', async (req, res) => { logger.info({ correlationId: req.correlationId, event: 'api.request', path: '/api/users' }); // ... }); ```

3️⃣ Modern Loggers

Winston (Node.js)

```typescript import winston from 'winston'; const logger = winston.createLogger({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info', format: winston.format.combine( winston.format.timestamp(), winston.format.json() ), transports: [ new winston.transports.Console(), new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/error.log', level: 'error' }), new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'logs/combined.log' }) ] }); logger.error('Payment failed', { userId: 123, amount: 99.99, error: err.message }); ```

Loguru (Python)

```python from loguru import logger logger.add("logs/app.log", rotation="500 MB", level="INFO") try: result = process_payment(user_id=123, amount=99.99) logger.info(f"Payment success: {result}") except Exception as e: logger.exception("Payment failed") ```

4️⃣ Error handling

Error handling global

```typescript // Express middleware app.use((err, req, res, next) => { logger.error({ correlationId: req.correlationId, event: 'api.error', path: req.path, method: req.method, error: { message: err.message, stack: err.stack, code: err.code } }); res.status(err.status || 500).json({ error: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'Internal Server Error' : err.message, correlationId: req.correlationId }); }); ```

Custom Error classes

```typescript class PaymentError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public userId: number, public amount: number) { super(message); this.name = 'PaymentError'; } } try { throw new PaymentError('Insufficient funds', 123, 99.99); } catch (err) { if (err instanceof PaymentError) { logger.error({ event: 'payment.failed', userId: err.userId, amount: err.amount, reason: err.message }); } } ```

5️⃣ Aggregation logs (Production)

ELK Stack

  • Elasticsearch: Stores logs
  • Logstash: Parse logs
  • Kibana: Visualization

Datadog / Sentry

```typescript import * as Sentry from '@sentry/node'; Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN }); app.use(Sentry.Handlers.requestHandler()); app.use(Sentry.Handlers.errorHandler()); ```

6️⃣ Golden Rules

  • ❌ Never passwords/tokens in logs
  • ✅ Logger request ID, user ID, timestamp
  • ✅ Structured JSON format
  • ✅ Rotation logs (max 500MB/file)
  • ✅ Alerts on critical errors (Slack/email)

🎯 Checklist logs

  • ✅ Log all try/catch
  • ✅ Correlation ID on queries
  • ✅ Log levels respected
  • ✅ No sensitive data
  • ✅ Centralized aggregation (ELK/Datadog)
  • ✅ Critical Error Alerts
> "Logs are the life insurance of production." 📝

title: Structuring a front project (React, Vue, Angular) properly
content:
Introduction: Organization = Maintainability

A well-structured front-end project remains understandable and scalable even after 2 years.

1️⃣ Structure by domain (Feature-based)

React + TypeScript

``` src/ ├── features/ │ ├── auth/ │ │ ├── components/ │ │ │ ├── LoginForm.tsx │ │ │ └── RegisterForm.tsx │ │ ├── hooks/ │ │ │ └── useAuth.ts │ │ ├── services/ │ │ │ └── authService.ts │ │ └── types/ │ │ └── user.types.ts │ ├── products/ │ │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── hooks/ │ │ └── services/ │ └── cart/ ├── shared/ │ ├── components/ (Button, Modal, Card) │ ├── hooks/ (useDebounce, useLocalStorage) │ ├── utils/ (formatDate, validateEmail) │ └── types/ (global types) ├── pages/ │ ├── HomePage.tsx │ ├── ProductsPage.tsx │ └── CheckoutPage.tsx ├── routes/ │ └── AppRoutes.tsx ├── store/ (Redux/Zustand) ├── api/ (axios config, interceptors) └── App.tsx ``` Advantages:
  • Code grouped by functionality
  • Easy to delete a feature
  • Avoid chaotic imports

2️⃣ Structure by type (Classic)

``` src/ ├── components/ │ ├── Button.tsx │ ├── Modal.tsx │ └── ProductCard.tsx ├── pages/ ├── hooks/ ├── services/ ├── utils/ └── types/ ``` When to use:
  • Small projects (<20 composants)
  • Simple apps (landing page, blog)

3️⃣ Naming rules

Components

```typescript // ✅ PascalCase for components export function UserProfile() { } export const ProductList = () => { }; // ✅ 1 composant = 1 fichier UserProfile.tsx ProductList.tsx ```

Hooks

```typescript // ✅ Prefix 'use' export function useAuth() { } export function useFetch(url: string) { } ```

Services

```typescript // ✅ Suffixe 'Service' export class AuthService { static login(email: string, password: string) { } } // authService.ts export const authService = { login: async (email, password) => { }, logout: async () => { } }; ```

4️⃣ Status management

Context API (local state)

```typescript // src/features/auth/context/AuthContext.tsx import { createContext, useContext, useState } from 'react'; const AuthContext = createContext(null); export function AuthProvider({ children }) { const [user, setUser] = useState(null); return ( {children} ); } export const useAuthContext = () => useContext(AuthContext); ```

Zustand (global state)

```typescript // src/store/useCartStore.ts import { create } from 'zustand'; export const useCartStore = create(set => ({ items: [], addItem: (item) => set(state => ({ items: [...state.items, item] })), removeItem: (id) => set(state => ({ items: state.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) })) })); ```

5️⃣ API Layer

Axios Configuration

```typescript // src/api/axios.ts import axios from 'axios'; export const api = axios.create({ baseURL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL, timeout: 10000 }); api.interceptors.request.use(config => { const token = localStorage.getItem('token'); if (token) config.headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`; return config; }); ```

Services

```typescript // src/features/products/services/productService.ts import { api } from '@/api/axios'; export const productService = { getAll: () => api.get('/products'), getById: (id: number) => api.get(`/products/${id}`), create: (data: CreateProductDto) => api.post('/products', data) }; ```

6️⃣ Path Aliases

tsconfig.json

```json { "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@/*": ["src/*"], "@/components/*": ["src/components/*"], "@/features/*": ["src/features/*"], "@/shared/*": ["src/shared/*"] } } } ```

Clean imports

```typescript // ❌ Imports relatifs sales import { Button } from '../../../shared/components/Button'; // ✅ Path aliases import { Button } from '@/shared/components/Button'; import { useAuth } from '@/features/auth/hooks/useAuth'; ```

🎯 Front Project Checklist

  • ✅ Feature-based structure (projects >20 components)
  • ✅ 1 component = 1 file
  • ✅ Clear names (PascalCase components, camelCase hooks)
  • ✅ Path aliases configured
  • ✅ Separate services (API layer)
  • ✅ Global isolated state (Zustand/Redux)
  • ✅ ESLint + Prettier configured
> “Solid front architecture = happy team.” 🎨

title: Why and how to do automatic linting / formatting (ESLint, Prettier, etc.)
content:
Introduction: Consistent Code = Effective Team

Linting + Formatting = automatic consistency, zero debate in code review on styles.

1️⃣ Linting: Detect errors

ESLint (JavaScript/TypeScript) detects:
  • Unused variables
  • Missing imports
  • Anti-patterns (== instead of ===)
  • Accessibility Violations

ESLint Installation

```bash npm install -D eslint @typescript-eslint/parser @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin npx eslint --init ```

Configuration .eslintrc.json

```json { "parser": "@typescript-eslint/parser", "extends": [ "eslint:recommended", "plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended", "plugin:react/recommended", "plugin:react-hooks/recommended" ], "rules": { "no-console": "warn", "no-unused-vars": "error", "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "warn" } } ```

Execution

```bash # Lint the whole project npx eslint src/ # Autofix erreurs simples npx eslint src/ --fix ```

2️⃣ Formatting: Uniform style

Prettier automatically formats:
  • Indentation (2 or 4 spaces)
  • Single/double quotes
  • Semicolon (presence/absence)
  • Max line width

Prettier Installation

```bash npm install -D prettier eslint-config-prettier eslint-plugin-prettier ```

Configuration .prettierrc

```json { "semi": true, "singleQuote": true, "tabWidth": 2, "trailingComma": "es5", "printWidth": 100 } ```

ESLint + Prettier integration

```json // .eslintrc.json { "extends": [ "eslint:recommended", "plugin:prettier/recommended" // Avoid conflicts ] } ```

3️⃣ Auto-format when saving (VS Code)

.vscode/settings.json

```json { "editor.formatOnSave": true, "editor.defaultFormatter": "esbenp.prettier-vscode", "editor.codeActionsOnSave": { "source.fixAll.eslint": true } } ```

4️⃣ Pre-commit hooks (Husky + lint-staged)

Force linting/formatting before commit.

Installation

```bash npm install -D husky lint-staged npx husky init ```

.husky/pre-commit

```bash #!/bin/sh npx lint-staged ```

package.json

```json { "lint-staged": { "*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}": [ "eslint --fix", "prettier --write" ], "*.{json,md,css}": [ "prettier --write" ] } } ``` Result: Unable to commit non-compliant code.

5️⃣ CI/CD: Lint in pipeline

GitHub Actions

```yaml name: Lint on: [pull_request] jobs: lint: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run format:check ```

package.json scripts

```json { "scripts": { "lint": "eslint src/", "lint:fix": "eslint src/ --fix", "format": "prettier --write "src/**/*.{js,ts,tsx,json,css,md}"", "format:check": "prettier --check "src/**/*.{js,ts,tsx,json,css,md}"" } } ```

6️⃣ Other languages

Python:
  • Linting: Pylint, Flake8, Ruff
  • Formatting: Black, autopep8
```bash # Install pip install black flake8 # Run black src/ flake8 src/ ``` Go:
  • go fmt (built-in)
  • golangci-lint
```bash go fmt ./... golangci-lint run ```

🎯 Benefits

  • ✅ Zero style debate in PR
  • ✅ Uniform code even with 10 devs
  • ✅ Bugs detected early (linting)
  • ✅ Quick onboarding (clear rules)
> “Prettier kills unnecessary debates.” 💅

title: Measure code quality: coverage, performance and maintainability
content:
Introduction: We only improve what we measure

Software quality is measured objectively via indicators and tools.

1️⃣ Code Coverage

Definition: Percentage of code executed by tests.

Jest (JavaScript/TypeScript)

```bash # Run tests with coverage npm test -- --coverage # Output File | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines ----------|---------|----------|---------|-------- user.ts | 85.7 | 75.0 | 80.0 | 85.0 ```

pytest-cov (Python)

```bash pytest --cov=src --cov-report=html # Generate htmlcov/index.html ``` Target: 80%+ (but 100%!= quality guaranteed).

2️⃣ Cyclomatic complexity

Definition: Number of independent paths in a function.

Example

```typescript // Complexité = 1 (simple) function add(a: number, b: number) { return a + b; } // Complexity = 4 (too high) function validateUser(user: User) { if (!user.email) throw new Error('Email required'); if (!user.password) throw new Error('Password required'); if (user.age < 18) throw new Error('Too young'); if (!user.terms) throw new Error('Accept terms'); } ``` Target: <10 par fonction.

Measurement with ESLint

```json // .eslintrc.json { "rules": { "complexity": ["warn", 10] } } ```

3️⃣ Maintainability Index

Microsoft formula:
  • Combines code volume, cyclomatic complexity, lines of code
  • Score 0-100 (>20 = OK, >85 = excellent)

SonarQube

```bash # Run SonarQube scan sonar-scanner \ -Dsonar.projectKey=my-project \ -Dsonar.sources=src \ -Dsonar.host.url=http://localhost:9000 ``` Metrics displayed:
  • Technical Debt (time to set)
  • Code Smells (anti-patterns)
  • Duplications
  • Maintainability Rating (A-E)

4️⃣ Performance Metrics

Lighthouse (Web)

```bash npm install -g lighthouse lighthouse https://example.com --view ``` Scores:
  • Performance (LCP, FID, CLS)
  • Accessibility
  • Best Practices
  • SEO

Backend Performance

```typescript // Measure endpoint performance import { performance } from 'perf_hooks'; app.get('/api/users', async (req, res) => { const start = performance.now(); const users = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users'); const duration = performance.now() - start; logger.info({ endpoint: '/users', duration }); res.json(users); }); ```

5️⃣ Monitoring Production

Datadog / New Relic

Traces:
  • Average latency (p50, p95, p99)
  • Throughput (req/s)
  • Error rate
  • DB query duration

Sentry (Error tracking)

```typescript import * as Sentry from '@sentry/node'; Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 0.1 // 10% traces }); app.use(Sentry.Handlers.requestHandler()); app.use(Sentry.Handlers.errorHandler()); ```

6️⃣ CI/CD Quality Gates

GitHub Actions

```yaml name: Quality on: [pull_request] jobs: quality: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - run: npm ci # Coverage check - run: npm test -- --coverage --coverageThreshold='{"global":{"statements":80}}' # SonarQube - uses: sonarsource/sonarqube-scan-action@master env: SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }} # Lighthouse CI - run: | npm run build lhci autorun ```

7️⃣ Dashboard centralization

Example stack:
  • SonarQube: Code quality
  • Grafana + Prometheus: Real-time metrics
  • Sentry: Errors
  • Lighthouse CI: Web performance

🎯 Recommended targets

| Metric | Target | |---------|--------| | Code Coverage | >80% | | Cyclomatic complexity | <10/fonction | | Maintainability Index | >65 | | Lighthouse Performance | >90 | | API Latency p95 | <500ms | | Error Rate | <1% | > "We only control what we measure." 📊

title: SOLID under the microscope: delving deeper into the principles of object design
content:
SOLID: Beyond the Basics

After having seen SOLID (article 31), we delve deeper with borderline cases, pitfalls and advanced applications.

1️⃣ SRP: Define “a responsibility”

Frequent trap

```typescript // ❌ SRP violation (User handles persistence + validation + email) class User { constructor(public email: string, public password: string) {} save() { db.query('INSERT INTO users...'); // Persistence } validate() { if (!this.email.includes('@')) throw new Error('Invalid email'); // Validation } sendWelcomeEmail() { mailer.send(this.email, 'Welcome!'); // Email } } ```

Advanced solution

```typescript // ✅ Chaque classe = 1 raison de changer class User { constructor(public email: string, public password: string) {} } class UserRepository { save(user: User): Promise { return db.query('INSERT INTO users (email, password) VALUES (?, ?)', [user.email, user.password]); } } class UserValidator { validate(user: User): void { if (!user.email.includes('@')) throw new ValidationError('Invalid email'); if (user.password.length < 8) throw new ValidationError('Password too short'); } } class UserNotifier { async sendWelcomeEmail(user: User): Promise { await mailer.send(user.email, 'welcome', { name: user.email }); } } ```

2️⃣ OCP: Extension without modification

Advanced strategy (Plugin system)

```typescript // ✅ Nouveau payment method = new class (zero changes to existing code) interface PaymentProcessor { process(amount: number): Promise; } class StripeProcessor implements PaymentProcessor { async process(amount: number) { return stripe.charge({ amount, currency: 'eur' }); } } class PayPalProcessor implements PaymentProcessor { async process(amount: number) { return paypal.createPayment({ amount }); } } // Nouveau : ajoute Crypto sans toucher code existant class CryptoProcessor implements PaymentProcessor { async process(amount: number) { return crypto.pay({ amount, wallet: '0x123...' }); } } class PaymentService { private processors = new Map(); register(name: string, processor: PaymentProcessor) { this.processors.set(name, processor); } async pay(method: string, amount: number) { const processor = this.processors.get(method); if (!processor) throw new Error(`Unknown method: ${method}`); return processor.process(amount); } } // Usage const service = new PaymentService(); service.register('stripe', new StripeProcessor()); service.register('paypal', new PayPalProcessor()); service.register('crypto', new CryptoProcessor()); // Extension ```

3️⃣ LSP: Borderline case

Classic Violation (Rectangle/Square)

```typescript // ❌ LSP violé : Square change comportement de Rectangle class Rectangle { constructor(protected width: number, protected height: number) {} setWidth(width: number) { this.width = width; } setHeight(height: number) { this.height = height; } area() { return this.width * this.height; } } class Square extends Rectangle { setWidth(width: number) { this.width = width; this.height = width; // ❌ Different behavior! } } // Test fails with Square function testRectangle(r: Rectangle) { r.setWidth(5); r.setHeight(10); console.assert(r.area() === 50); // ❌ Square area = 100 ! } ```

Solution: Composition > Inheritance

```typescript // ✅ No misleading inheritance interface Shape { area(): number; } class Rectangle implements Shape { constructor(private width: number, private height: number) {} area() { return this.width * this.height; } } class Square implements Shape { constructor(private side: number) {} area() { return this.side ** 2; } } ```

4️⃣ ISP: Fine interfaces

Problem

```typescript // ❌ Fat interface: forces unnecessary implementation interface Worker { work(): void; eat(): void; sleep(): void; } class Robot implements Worker { work() { console.log('Working'); } eat() { throw new Error('Robots don't eat'); } // ❌ Inutile sleep() { throw new Error('Robots don't sleep'); } // ❌ Inutile } ```

Solution: Segregated interfaces

```typescript // ✅ Interfaces fines interface Workable { work(): void; } interface Eatable { eat(): void; } interface Sleepable { sleep(): void; } class Human implements Workable, Eatable, Sleepable { work() { console.log('Working'); } eat() { console.log('Eating'); } sleep() { console.log('Sleeping'); } } class Robot implements Workable { work() { console.log('Working 24/7'); } } ```

5️⃣ DIP: Dependency Injection

Problem

```typescript // ❌ Concrete dependency (hard to test) class UserService { private repo = new MySQLUserRepository(); // ❌ Tight coupling async createUser(email: string) { return this.repo.save({ email }); } } ```

Solution: Dependency Injection

```typescript // ✅ Abstract dependency interface UserRepository { save(user: User): Promise; } class MySQLUserRepository implements UserRepository { async save(user: User) { /* MySQL logic */ } } class PostgresUserRepository implements UserRepository { async save(user: User) { /* Postgres logic */ } } class UserService { constructor(private repo: UserRepository) {} // ✅ Inject abstraction async createUser(email: string) { return this.repo.save({ email }); } } // Usage const service = new UserService(new MySQLUserRepository()); // Testing const mockRepo: UserRepository = { save: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined) }; const testService = new UserService(mockRepo); ```

🎯 SOLID in practice

  • SRP: Class changes for 1 reason only
  • OCP: Extension via new classes, no modification
  • LSP: Composition > Inheritance if in doubt
  • ISP: Several small interfaces > 1 large
  • DIP: Inject abstractions, not implementations
> “SOLID = discipline, not dogma.” 🏗️

title: Design Patterns: catalog of essential patterns
content:
Design Patterns: Common Vocabulary

Design Patterns are reusable solutions to recurring problems. In-depth catalog.

1️⃣ Creational Patterns

Singleton (Single instance)

When: 1 single global instance (DB connection, config). ```typescript class Database { private static instance: Database; private constructor() {} // Private constructor static getInstance(): Database { if (!Database.instance) { Database.instance = new Database(); } return Database.instance; } query(sql: string) { /* ... */ } } // Usage const db1 = Database.getInstance(); const db2 = Database.getInstance(); console.log(db1 === db2); // true (same instance) ```

Factory Method (Delegated creation)

When: Complex creation or variants. ```typescript interface Vehicle { drive(): void; } class Car implements Vehicle { drive() { console.log('Driving car'); } } class Bike implements Vehicle { drive() { console.log('Riding bike'); } } class VehicleFactory { static create(type: 'car' | 'bike'): Vehicle { switch (type) { case 'car': return new Car(); case 'bike': return new Bike(); default: throw new Error('Unknown type'); } } } // Usage const vehicle = VehicleFactory.create('car'); vehicle.drive(); ```

Builder (Step by step construction)

When: Complex object with multiple options. ```typescript class HttpRequest { constructor( public url: string, public method: string = 'GET', public headers: Record = {}, public body?: any ) {} } class HttpRequestBuilder { private url = ''; private method = 'GET'; private headers: Record = {}; private body?: any; setUrl(url: string) { this.url = url; return this; // Fluent interface } setMethod(method: string) { this.method = method; return this; } setHeader(key: string, value: string) { this.headers[key] = value; return this; } setBody(body: any) { this.body = body; return this; } build(): HttpRequest { return new HttpRequest(this.url, this.method, this.headers, this.body); } } // Usage const request = new HttpRequestBuilder() .setUrl('/api/users') .setMethod('POST') .setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json') .setBody({ name: 'John' }) .build(); ```

2️⃣ Structural Patterns

Adapt (Interface conversion)

When: Interface legacy system with new code. ```typescript // Old system class OldLogger { logMessage(msg: string) { console.log(`[OLD] ${msg}`); } } // New interface interface Logger { log(level: string, message: string): void; } // Adapter class LoggerAdapter implements Logger { constructor(private oldLogger: OldLogger) {} log(level: string, message: string) { this.oldLogger.logMessage(`[${level}] ${message}`); } } // Usage const logger: Logger = new LoggerAdapter(new OldLogger()); logger.log('INFO', 'Application started'); ```

Decorator (Dynamic addition of behaviors)

When: Add functionality without modifying original class. ```typescript interface Coffee { cost(): number; description(): string; } class SimpleCoffee implements Coffee { cost() { return 5; } description() { return 'Coffee'; } } // Decorators class MilkDecorator implements Coffee { constructor(private coffee: Coffee) {} cost() { return this.coffee.cost() + 1; } description() { return `${this.coffee.description()} + Milk`; } } class SugarDecorator implements Coffee { constructor(private coffee: Coffee) {} cost() { return this.coffee.cost() + 0.5; } description() { return `${this.coffee.description()} + Sugar`; } } // Usage let coffee: Coffee = new SimpleCoffee(); coffee = new MilkDecorator(coffee); coffee = new SugarDecorator(coffee); console.log(coffee.description()); // "Coffee + Milk + Sugar" console.log(coffee.cost()); // 6.5 ```

Facade (Simplified interface)

When: Simplify access to complex system. ```typescript class CPU { freeze() { console.log('CPU freeze'); } execute() { console.log('CPU execute'); } } class Memory { load() { console.log('Memory load'); } } class HardDrive { read() { console.log('HDD read'); } } // Facade class ComputerFacade { private cpu = new CPU(); private memory = new Memory(); private hdd = new HardDrive(); start() { this.hdd.read(); this.memory.load(); this.cpu.freeze(); this.cpu.execute(); } } // Usage (simplifié) const computer = new ComputerFacade(); computer.start(); ```

3️⃣ Behavioral Patterns

Observer (Pub/Sub)

When: Automatic notifications (events, state management). ```typescript interface Observer { update(data: any): void; } class Subject { private observers: Observer[] = []; attach(observer: Observer) { this.observers.push(observer); } notify(data: any) { this.observers.forEach(o => o.update(data)); } } class EmailNotifier implements Observer { update(data: any) { console.log(`Email sent: ${data}`); } } class SMSNotifier implements Observer { update(data: any) { console.log(`SMS sent: ${data}`); } } // Usage const userCreated = new Subject(); userCreated.attach(new EmailNotifier()); userCreated.attach(new SMSNotifier()); userCreated.notify('New user: John'); ```

Strategy (Interchangeable Algorithms)

When: Multiple algorithm variations. ```typescript interface CompressionStrategy { compress(data: string): string; } class ZipCompression implements CompressionStrategy { compress(data: string) { return `[ZIP] ${data}`; } } class RarCompression implements CompressionStrategy { compress(data: string) { return `[RAR] ${data}`; } } class FileCompressor { constructor(private strategy: CompressionStrategy) {} setStrategy(strategy: CompressionStrategy) { this.strategy = strategy; } compress(file: string) { return this.strategy.compress(file); } } // Usage const compressor = new FileCompressor(new ZipCompression()); console.log(compressor.compress('data.txt')); // [ZIP] data.txt compressor.setStrategy(new RarCompression()); console.log(compressor.compress('data.txt')); // [RAR] data.txt ```

Command (Action encapsulation)

When: Undo/Redo, queues, logging. ```typescript interface Command { execute(): void; undo(): void; } class Light { on() { console.log('Light ON'); } off() { console.log('Light OFF'); } } class LightOnCommand implements Command { constructor(private light: Light) {} execute() { this.light.on(); } undo() { this.light.off(); } } class LightOffCommand implements Command { constructor(private light: Light) {} execute() { this.light.off(); } undo() { this.light.on(); } } class RemoteControl { private history: Command[] = []; execute(command: Command) { command.execute(); this.history.push(command); } undo() { const command = this.history.pop(); command?.undo(); } } // Usage const light = new Light(); const remote = new RemoteControl(); remote.execute(new LightOnCommand(light)); // Light ON remote.execute(new LightOffCommand(light)); // Light OFF remote.undo(); // Light ON (undo last) ```

🎯 When to use?

  • Singleton: Config, DB pool, cache
  • Factory: Object variants (user types, vehicles)
  • Builder: Complex objects (HTTP requests, queries)
  • Adapt: Legacy/3rd party integration
  • Decorator: Middlewares, logging, caching
  • Observer: Events, reactive programming (React, Vue)
  • Strategy: Payments, sorting, compression
  • Command: Undo/Redo, task queues
> “Patterns = solutions, not obligations.” 🎨
